approval.note: Sol approved this exact Gate 4.5 manifest on 2026-08-21. Approval covers the reviewed artifact as it stands: no source hash, artifact hash, scope definition, classification, projection text, review mapping or repository identity was altered by the approval. Scopes classified CLASSIFIED_NOT_APPROVED (e.g. HattonHills) remain unapproved and continue to fail closed. The engine MUST still refuse to project any entry while state != APPROVED.

SOURCE_DERIVED.meaning: Text derived from an approved instruction source in the target repository. Every statement traces to a named source file, source SHA-256 and source section.
SOURCE_DERIVED.required_result: ZERO matches. A match is fixed by changing the content, never by weakening the pattern set.

DISPATCHER_AUTHORED.meaning: Refusal, prohibition, framing and policy text written and owned by the dispatcher. Not imported project content.
DISPATCHER_AUTHORED.trusted_by: its own artifact SHA-256 recorded in this manifest, plus dispatcher source review
DISPATCHER_AUTHORED.rule: MUST NOT be merged into a SOURCE_DERIVED file. This is a provenance distinction, not a scanner exception (GATE4.5-RULINGS.md §2).

strict_secret_operator_v1.note: Applied to SOURCE_DERIVED artifacts only. Patterns 1-6 are case-insensitive; pattern 7 is case-sensitive.

behavioural_configuration_policy.eligible: Behavioural configuration defining application semantics, invariants, timeouts, limits, protocol behaviour, parsing behaviour, safety thresholds or compatibility constraints. Names and values may be projected as implementation facts.
behavioural_configuration_policy.secret_values: NEVER, under any circumstances, in any artifact.
behavioural_configuration_policy.mandatory_framing_text: These values are behavioural constraints / observed runtime decisions. Do not change production configuration. If implementation requires changing one, report the implication to Sol.
behavioural_configuration_policy.framing_location: Carried verbatim in the DISPATCHER_AUTHORED policy artifact of every scope whose projection names such values, because SOURCE_DERIVED and DISPATCHER_AUTHORED text must not be commingled (rulings §2). The policy artifact is always emitted immediately before its source artifact, so the framing precedes the values in the worker's context.

repositories.identity_check: toplevel AND git_dir AND origin_url AND root_commit must ALL match at dispatch; otherwise ProjectGuidanceRepositoryMismatch

source_resolution.rule: Sources are resolved as toplevel + the exact repository-relative path recorded in an entry. There is NO glob-based nearest-CLAUDE.md discovery and no recursive instruction-file search for resolution (GATE4.5-RULINGS.md §3).

shadow_source_hazard.note: A DIFFERENT-hashed shadow copy of Kavya/CLAUDE.md exists inside an in-repo worktree, and ~30 more sibling copies exist under /home/dev/worktrees/. Neither may ever become a guidance source. This must have a hard regression test.

unapproved_file_discovery.purpose: DEFAULT-DENY verification only. It never selects or resolves a source; resolution is manifest-pinned.

scope_map.note: Ordered, source-controlled, exact repository-relative directory prefixes. Nearest-scope inheritance is encoded here as DATA: the engine performs a longest-matching-prefix lookup over this list. No glob. No model. The six prefixes are mutually non-prefixing today, so the longest match is unique; if a nested scope is ever added, select ONLY the longest match plus the root entry.

unapproved_scope_behaviour.rule: GATE4.5-RULINGS.md §7 — a task whose allowed_paths intersect a scope with no approved curated projection MUST fail closed. Silent root-only fallback is forbidden.

graph_refresh_gate.read_only_exploration: ALWAYS ELIGIBLE — reading graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md and running graphify query|path|explain is unconditional and lives in the root source projection block [R2].

emission.note: Fixed, reproducible order. For each selected entry the DISPATCHER_AUTHORED policy artifact is emitted first, then its SOURCE_DERIVED artifact. The graph-refresh clause is emitted last.
order: for each selected subscope in scope_map declaration order: entry.policy_artifact then entry.source_artifact
emission.worker_and_review_are_disjoint: A worker never receives a review artifact and Fable never receives a worker artifact. The two artifact sets are disjoint files with disjoint hashes.

pg.fva.root.source_relationship_note: Root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are NOT aliases and are NOT claimed to be synchronised. Both are independent reviewed sources; the projection is derived from both. Non-identity is expected and is NOT a Gate 4.5 failure (GATE4.5-RULINGS.md §6). Both hashes are pinned; a change to EITHER invalidates this projection until reapproved.

failure_semantics.condition: ORDERING (Sol ruling 2026-08-20): when more than one condition below is true for the same edit, the MORE PRECISE error is reported. Editing one half of an ALIASES_BYTE_IDENTICAL pair is simultaneously an alias divergence and a source hash mismatch; ProjectGuidanceDrift fires first because "these approved aliases no longer agree" is operationally more useful than "one source hash changed". Both are fail-closed and both return the task to Sol. This documents the intended behaviour of the shipped engine; do not change the code to match older prose that listed SourceChanged first.
repository identity mismatch on any of toplevel / git dir / origin url / root commit
an ALIASES_BYTE_IDENTICAL pair no longer has equal hashes
failure_semantics.behaviour: fail closed (addendum §7 V1 preference); evaluated BEFORE the generic source-hash condition below

failure_semantics.condition: a source file SHA-256 differs from this manifest and the file is not half of a diverged alias pair
root pair acquires CONFLICTING eligible guidance
failure_semantics.behaviour: fail closed. Mere non-identity of the root pair is acknowledged in this manifest and does NOT fail (rulings §6).

an allowed_path resolves outside the repository toplevel, contains an escape after normalisation, or lands under a deny prefix or deny absolute tree
